## Design

### 2026-10-18 – First, I researched how 3D printers actually work. I found a comparison chart and watched multiple videos on the Voron and Core XY printers. I liked the Voron because all the motion was in the gantry,

**2.92h**

First, I researched how 3D printers actually work. I found a comparison chart and watched multiple videos on the Voron and Core XY printers. I liked the Voron because all the motion was in the gantry, making the model much smaller than an actual 3d printer, but this would mean I would have to design more complex parts, and I only have beginner CAD skills.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/1510fd2d587a7394b25f7b04352cb376eea8c4c9f456e380be1e5fb42988ae43.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/4a770db10ecc6d8c008a014b86fdac77fa0e987ef95b49bcd144d42dfb2d73d8.png)

I found that most printers used belts to move, linear rails for low friction, and rods for rigidity and support. For my model, I decided to make just the rods so that someone could move the carriage freely without modeling complex components or adding extra friction.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/748dc6a9cd4988e2841e504a0bd7b8a774ab2d48c4586e9cf87f5ef7e2e96ba4.png)

Then I started modeling and saw that my design looked a lot like (_every other CoreXY _), the FlashForge AD5M. I had only done the top gantry, but the boxy shape and the color I chose for the model reminded me of it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/ba615b2422c3b6f60b5b7b0131e6803bdee955fd88594c77a717c6d3242c1ab7.png)

My next goal is to make the body and the base, which should be easy. I will need to do more research on how to build it and figure out what I want it to look like.

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/ba2be3e8-71b7-4341-a704-addcfea3a22f/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-18 – After making the top and gantry, I researched different frame designs. Most inexpensive printers use an open "wire frame" design with 2020 aluminum extrusion, while higher-end ones use molded plastic,

**1.58h**

After making the top and gantry, I researched different frame designs. Most inexpensive printers use an open "wire frame" design with 2020 aluminum extrusion, while higher-end ones use molded plastic, acrylic, or steel. I also chose to do an open printer because there was no need for the added complexity of an enclosure, and it would mess up the easy access to move the gantry.

![OIP](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/872fe4f2ed076edc7adb35b6d3146b22da3ba63daeb8ddc95c764acc62441478.webp)

Because I was leaning more into the Flashforge as my reference, I decided to go with a design that would use plastic. It is still an open design with no back plate, because there are no electronics or other heavy parts.

I found this comparison picture of the 5M and 5M Pro, and I'm going for more of a 5M-style printer that's a little more open.

![OIP](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/26767f96d19de0c9ff5c75d96e48bd410086206194816cf2060df31c76d77119.webp)

[Timelapse](https://lookout.hackclub.com/api/media/9a883ddd-0faa-4cca-a158-9addd4d0a5a2/video.mp4)

### 2026-10-18 – After making the frame, I did quite a bit of research on how to make the bed move up and down. Printers use a lead screw attached to the stepper motor with a coupler, so all I would have to do is figu

**2.65h**

After making the frame, I did quite a bit of research on how to make the bed move up and down. Printers use a lead screw attached to the stepper motor with a coupler, so all I would have to do is figure out how to make a lead screw turn....

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/989a8febe3c6d983f32a19a26726e02eb3cd66aa631aa004926f2a8bab895352.png)

My first thought was to use gears, but I do not know how to make good gears. Then I looked at using a worm gear drive or rack and pinion, but these would add complexity, size, and a backplate. I wanted everything to be easily printable, so I did not add any mechanism to move the bed; It would also be like the rest of the design because the x and y axes don't have any mechanism to move them either.

![OIP](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/465e58074d0d3b47645a42a1e84ff0cb478c516ec29b6f99918079ca52059ea8.webp)

I went back and added the build plate because I wanted the full experience of having a 3D printer. At first, I tried to design a plate with grooves to help keep the build plate in place, based on magnetic beds, but those grooves would stick up above the bed. Because I am printing the bed upside down, the clips would add support that would be really hard to get off. They would also be extra pieces that I don't actually need to print. So I changed from clips to a drop-in style build plate because :
1. It keeps the bed the same size
2. It helps to align the bed to the bed mount
3. It keeps the bed and build plate printable without supports.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/3d341b26efba00b10f6f5b0a7dab35d726f2ce057dbffaac3482b4ee91753a43.webp)

![OIP](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/8c24f91f5be7942d69ed8f11484d925a814e7f175b8226270a9964ef52a8ba9d.webp)

Next is adding the extruder or some tip that may or may not be functional.

### 2026-10-18 – So I know I can't model the complexities of a full toolhead, so I researched different nozzle designs. The most common is the standard brass nozzle. There are also stainless- and hardened-steel nozzle

**1.75h**

So I know I can't model the complexities of a full toolhead, so I researched different nozzle designs. The most common is the standard brass nozzle. There are also stainless- and hardened-steel nozzles, but I could change the color to represent each nozzle type.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/fee1e9be03e64e62641a37dc8de2d522cec7f06016adca160d21dd2698eec24e.png)

That led me on a tangent about different attachments for the printer, such as a CNC, laser engraving, or even a pen plotter attachment. I thought it would be cool to make a pen plotter, because even though it would be entirely useless, it would look really cool.

![laser-cutting-vs-cnc-machining-wooden-decorative-panels-birch-plywood-manufactur](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/00624b50efc07f90aa62b682fdedfeaf416508344a9edfed288129ca813605e6.jpg)

![P1655305](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/G3uMJ4kUC5n21VcwynuADM4K8m3ol7fg/916136a21aad141c421d914edecd38d7c948760d4d39ffcc75a4071e3499d5f6.jpg)
